text:
Google has run two core updates and three spam updates this year.

Spam updates go after shortcuts. Fake reviews. Stuffed business names. Junk pages.

When those businesses drop, somebody moves up.

Be the one doing the boring work when it happens.

Plumber in Parramatta. Eleven years, two vans. The bloke down the road sits above him on Google Maps every time.

His name on Google: "Western Sydney Plumbing - Emergency Plumber Parramatta 24/7 Blocked Drains".

(Bit long for a van door.)

"Should I copy him?"

No.

Roofer in Cannington gets a Facebook lead at 9pm.

Rings back at 11 the next morning.

"Already booked someone, mate."

Meta now lets people pick an appointment time straight after your lead form.

Let them book while they're keen.

Cafe owner in West End, Brisbane: "We dropped on Google this week. Do we rebuild the website?"

Rankings bounce around while an update rolls out.

Wait until Google says it's finished. Then wait another week. Then look at the numbers.

Panic edits cost more than updates.

Want "emergency plumber" to bring you calls on Google?

Leave it out of your business name. Google says extra words in there can get your profile suspended.

Put it in your categories, services, description and photos of real jobs.

About an hour. Most owners never finish it.

I lose some jobs on the first phone call.

Cafe owner in Fremantle wants page one by Christmas. I tell him I can't promise that. Nobody honest can.

He signs with someone who said yes.

I'd rather lose the job than lie to get it.
